articles.title: 2025: A Year of Cracks in U.S. Support for Israel and the Rise of the Palestinian Voice in America
articles.summary: The year 2025 marked significant shifts in the United States regarding public opinion and political dynamics surrounding the Palestinian issue. A growing public opposition to foreign wars, particularly the Israeli war in Gaza, was reflected in opinion polls showing a decline in support for U.S. military and political backing of Israel. This shift, driven by widespread media coverage of civilian casualties, humanitarian blockade, and sustained violence, empowered anti-war movements and expanded the space for public criticism of U.S. policy. A major milestone was the release of Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khleif after months of detention by U.S. immigration authorities, following a large-scale public pressure campaign. Additionally, several pro-Palestinian activists, students, and journalists were released, signaling a weakening of political repression. Concurrently, the influence of the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) declined, with multiple candidates and members of Congress rejecting its financial support and voting against its positions. This shift reflects a broader public awareness of AIPAC’s role in shaping U.S. foreign policy and growing political courage to challenge it openly. On the local level, Zharan Mammadli’s victory in the New York City mayoral race—campaigning on social justice and opposition to war—brought the Palestinian cause to the forefront of one of America’s most politically and financially connected cities, fueling demands to divest from companies complicit in Israeli military actions. Internationally, the 'Global Solidarity Flotilla' sailed toward Gaza, drawing attention to the blockade and amplifying the Palestinian narrative in the U.S. Despite arrests and obstruction, the flotilla reinvigorated public discourse. A pivotal moment occurred in December 2025, when over 40 protesters gathered in sub-zero temperatures outside the Illinois State Investment Board meeting, demanding divestment from Israeli bonds and companies linked to the occupation. Led by Chicago-based groups including AWC-Chicago and BDS-Chicago—affiliated with the U.S. Palestinian Community Network (USPCN)—the protest grew to include over 55 organizations across Illinois. Protesters highlighted that Illinois invests approximately $100 million in Israeli bonds, while Israel has caused a man-made famine affecting over two million people in Gaza. Activists criticized the allocation of public funds to defense contractors like Boeing, Lockheed Martin, and Caterpillar, which profit from violence in Gaza. Inside the meeting, representatives delivered research documenting the complicity of these investments in occupation and repression. When six protesters peacefully chained themselves to the chamber, they were forcibly removed by Illinois state police, underscoring the contradiction between democratic rhetoric and repressive practice. The protest concluded with a reaffirmation by Hossam Mardah of USPCN that 2025, though marked by repression at the beginning, ended with a more organized and determined movement. The year thus represented a turning point in the U.S., where public solidarity with Palestine evolved from isolated actions into a sustained, organized political and economic force.

articles.title: Global Public Outcry in 2025 Against Israel’s Gaza Offensive
articles.summary: In 2025, global public opinion expressed strong and widespread protests against Israel's military actions in the Gaza Strip, which the article claims have amounted to genocide since October 2023, resulting in over 70,000 deaths. Multinational demonstrations took place in cities across Europe, North America, Australia, and the Middle East, with participants demanding sanctions, a red line against Israel, and an end to military support. Events such as the 'Red Line' protests in Amsterdam (250,000 attendees) and Berlin (where protesters painted government buildings red), a 100,000-strong march in Sydney, and a large protest in New York during Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s UN visit highlighted global mobilization. Student activism at top universities in the U.S., including Columbia and Harvard, continued despite pressure from the Trump administration. International humanitarian efforts, including the Global Sumud flotilla and the 'Freedom Flotilla' coalition, attempted to deliver aid to Gaza, facing Israeli attacks and arrests. Protests also targeted companies linked to Israel, with Microsoft facing employee-led demonstrations in August. Cultural figures, including Billy Eilish, Cillian Murphy, Joaquin Phoenix, and Hannah Einbinder (who shouted 'Free Palestine' at the Emmys), joined the movement. Over 4,000 celebrities signed a statement refusing collaboration with Israeli studios. The 'No Music for Genocide' campaign led to the blocking of music on Israeli streaming platforms by over 1,000 artists. Israeli artists Nemo and Charlie McGettigan returned their Eurovision trophies in protest. Footballer Mohamed Salah criticized UEFA for omitting the cause of a Palestinian player’s death in condolences. Lewis Hamilton condemned the deaths of thousands of children in Gaza. Polls from Pew Research Center (59% negative view of Israel), YouGov (recorded negative sentiment in Western Europe), and the Washington Post (61% of U.S. Jews believe Israel committed war crimes, 39% called it genocide) confirmed a significant shift in global public perception.

articles.title: Lapid: Israel's Shift Toward a U.S.-Dependent State and Egypt’s Role in Gaza Management
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid expressed concern during a speech before the Knesset's Subcommittee on Foreign Relations and Public Diplomacy regarding Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's official visit to the United States, where Netanyahu is scheduled to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump. Lapid stated that Netanyahu is arriving at the meeting without a clear vision for Gaza, warning that without a defined strategy, others—particularly the U.S.—will shape Israel’s policy. He reiterated his long-standing proposal that Egypt should manage Gaza, arguing that if Israel lacks ideas, the U.S. will impose its own, leaving Israel politically paralyzed. Lapid emphasized that Israel risks becoming a 'dependent state' under Washington’s influence. The meeting is seen as a pivotal moment in U.S.-Israel relations, especially as the current U.S.-Israel security cooperation agreement is set to expire in 2028. The Jerusalem Post previously urged swift negotiation of a new agreement, calling for a reevaluation of outdated recommendations from the 2023 12-day war with Iran, particularly those related to the new security cooperation framework.

articles.title: Jasim Al-Azzawi articles
articles.summary: The article is a curated list of op-ed pieces by Jasim Al-Azzawi, published between September 2025 and December 2025, covering a range of geopolitical and international affairs topics. Key themes include the Middle East conflict, with articles such as 'The war no one declares: Inside the Mossad–Iran shadow conflict' (03.12.2025), 'The Abraham Accords gambit: Washington’s high-stakes balancing act in the Middle East' (06.12.2025), and 'The vanishing future of the Arab world: climate, corruption, and the AI divide' (28.11.2025). Other pieces critique U.S. foreign policy, such as 'America at the edge: Lessons from Rome, warnings from history' (30.11.2025), 'US public opinion on Israel is changing, US policy will have to as well' (22.09.2025), and 'The Palestinian recognition cascade: America’s diplomatic isolation' (22.09.2025). Several articles target Israeli leadership, including 'Thank you, Netanyahu, for stripping Zionism of its lies and revealing Israel’s odious nature' (26.11.2025) and 'Netanyahu, you crossed the Rubicon' (12.09.2025). The list also includes commentary on regional dynamics, such as 'Iraq’s tightrope walk sharpens between American security and Iranian influence' (24.11.2025), 'Hizballah’s last stand: Disarmament, defiance, and Tehran’s shadow over Lebanon' (23.10.2025), and 'Egypt’s silent crisis: A paradox of stability and tension' (06.09.2025). A final note mentions U.S. pressure on Iraq to dismantle pro-Iranian paramilitary groups, indicating a strategic shift in Washington’s approach. The compilation was published on December 14, 2025, at 06:44, sourced from qoshe.com.
